sections.heading: The honest answer to 'where can I fly cheaply from London'
sections.body:
London has six airports, which means more cheap flight options than almost any city in Europe. The trick is knowing which airport to use for which destination, and when to go.

The answer to 'where can I fly cheaply from London' changes by month, by day of week, and by which airline is running a sale. But some patterns hold consistently. Portugal is always well-priced from London. Eastern Europe is consistently cheap from Stansted. The Canary Islands are competitive year-round from Gatwick. And there are always a handful of routes each month where an airline has more seats than it expected to sell — and those excess seats get priced to clear.

The table below shows what's cheapest from London's airports today, updated every few hours.

sections.heading: Routes from London that are reliably cheap
sections.body:
London Stansted to Faro, Portugal (FAO) — Ryanair: Often around £55–75 one-way outside school holidays. Faro is the gateway to the Algarve — arguably the best beach region in southern Europe for the quality-to-price ratio. The water is cooler than the Med but the beaches (Meia Praia, Praia da Marinha, the Ria Formosa lagoons) are extraordinary. May, June and September are the sweet spot: warm, open and far quieter than August.

London Stansted to Krakow, Poland (KRK) — Ryanair: Often around £35–55 one-way outside peak weeks. Krakow is one of the best city breaks in Europe at any price, but at £35 it's remarkable. The old town is one of the most intact medieval city centres on the continent. The food is excellent. Auschwitz-Birkenau is 90 minutes by bus and should be on everyone's list. Budget £40/day on the ground and eat and drink well.

London Gatwick to Tenerife (TFS) — easyJet: Often around £80–105 one-way outside school holidays. Tenerife is warm all year and much cheaper outside July, August and Christmas. Teide, the Masca gorge, Loro Parque if you have children. The south of the island has good beaches and a developed resort infrastructure. A week in spring or autumn costs far less than the same trip in August.

London Luton to Tirana, Albania (TIA) — Wizz Air: Often around £40–65 one-way outside summer. Albania is one of Europe's most underrated destinations — Adriatic coast beaches, remarkably good food, and almost no tourist infrastructure pricing yet. A coastal week in late spring at Ksamil or Himarë costs roughly what the same trip would have cost in Montenegro five years ago.

sections.heading: Which London airport for which destination
sections.body:
This matters more than most people realise. The cheapest flight to Faro might be from Stansted, but if you live in West London, the Stansted Express and a Tube journey adds 90 minutes and £25 each way to your trip. The right airport depends on where you're starting from.

If you're in Central or East London: Stansted for Ryanair routes (Krakow, Porto, Seville, Warsaw, Faro, Naples, Eindhoven). Gatwick for easyJet European routes (Tenerife, Malaga, Lanzarote, Alicante, Barcelona, Nice). Both have direct fast trains — Stansted Express 47 minutes, Gatwick Express 30 minutes from Victoria.

If you're in North or West London: Luton for Wizz Air and Ryanair (Budapest, Bucharest, Warsaw, Tirana). Heathrow for BA and long-haul. The Luton routes are consistently the cheapest but the airport is the least pleasant of London's main airports — budget extra time.

If you're in South London: Gatwick is your airport. It's 30 minutes from Victoria. Don't pay for a Stansted Express journey from South London when easyJet from Gatwick is often within £10–15 of the same Ryanair fare from Stansted.

The rule: don't choose the airport with the cheapest headline fare without adding the journey cost. A £35 Ryanair fare from Stansted that costs £30 in trains from your home is a £65 fare. A £50 easyJet fare from Gatwick that's 30 minutes away is a better deal.

sections.heading: The best times to fly cheaply from London
sections.body:
Bank holiday weekends carry a premium. Friday departures and Monday returns cost more, so fly out on the Tuesday or Wednesday before, or the week after, and the same route is often 20-30% cheaper.

School holidays set the price. Half-terms, Easter, late July and August, and Christmas push up fares on family routes like Malaga, Palma and Faro. Outside those weeks, London has some of the cheapest flights in Europe. Our month-by-month guide shows when each month is cheap.

Pick the less obvious destination. Tirana, Varna, Skopje, Catania and Naples tend to hold their prices better through busy weekends than Malaga, Ibiza or Mallorca.
